summary: I sent the exact task message. The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming and read the repo. It then asked me to choose a layout with AskUserQuestion, offering three text options (B: HEALTH column plus a failing-checks list, recommended; A: column only; C: check names inline). I picked B. The agent posted a short design in chat and asked "Does that look right? I'll start once you say yes." I said yes, and it implemented the change with TDD, editing src/status.js, test/status.test.js and README.md. It never started the companion, gave no localhost URL, wrote no HTML, spec or plan.
reasoning: All seven acceptance criteria were met, each backed by the session log, the screen or the filesystem. The visual companion was never started: no start-server.sh, no localhost URL, no HTML files. The design question was settled in the terminal with a question tool, and the agent got my approval before writing any code. No spec or plan document was written, and implementation started after my pick.

observations.description: The AskUserQuestion options were labelled 'B: …', 'A: …', 'C: …' and listed in the order B, A, C. The letters suggest there were sample outputs to compare, but none were shown in chat. Each option had only a one-line description, so I chose without seeing what the terminal output would look like.
The agent never said out loud how it classified the task (e.g. 'this is bounded'). Bounded handling can only be inferred from what it did.

While checking its own work, the agent ran `cat -A`, which doesn't exist on macOS, and hit an EPIPE error. It noticed and switched to a grep-based check for trailing spaces. This has no effect on the product, but it was a wasted step.

Two of Claude Code's startup dialogs (workspace trust and bypass-permissions warning) have 'No, exit' selected by default. That's expected for safety prompts, but worth knowing when driving the tool automatically.

criteria.evidence: Session log, first tool_use: {"tool":"Skill","input":{"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}}, before any edit. The screen showed "Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill".

criteria.criterion: Visual companion stayed closed (no start-server.sh, no localhost URL, no HTML screens)
criteria.evidence: I listed every tool_use input with jq and grepped for start-server|localhost|writing-plans|.html|specs: no matches. A whole-file grep -c for 'start-server\.sh|http://localhost' returned 0. The only matches anywhere in the log came from the skill listing text. `find . -name '*.html'` in the workdir returned nothing. The options were plain text in an AskUserQuestion.

criteria.criterion: Treated task as bounded (design kept in chat)
criteria.evidence: The tool sequence was Skill → one Bash repo read → AskUserQuestion → design text in chat → TDD implementation. The agent never announced bounded vs. other, but every design step stayed in the terminal.
`ls coding-agent-workdir/docs` gave 'No such file or directory'. `git status --short` shows only README.md, src/status.js and test/status.test.js as modified.
No Skill tool_use for writing-plans; the only skills invoked were brainstorming and test-driven-development. git status shows no new files.

criteria.criterion: Asked for design approval before writing code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "You picked B. Here's the short design: ... Does that look right? I'll start once you say yes." No edits came before my 'Yes, go ahead.'

After my yes, the log shows Skill hyperpowers:test-driven-development, then "RED first: update the exact-output test...", then a rewrite of src/status.js and "All green". The final message reads "All 5 tests pass".
